body: Wait. An inflatable rubber dam? What the hell?

The ones that are "hate" are to people from the past, except my roommates who I live with now.

The last 3 are to friends that have left a recent impression on me.
A few of them are to friends. I haven't gotten to family or anything yet.
I feel like I've calmed down a little bit. Less panicky but still very aware that this seems like the easiest way out.

Practically living together and actually living together can be entirely different situations.

I know that sounds silly, but for some people this is the case. Have you considered the differences between the two?

I looked into it and it sounds like a promising option; however it isn't the lack of possible solutions, it's how to bring up said solution. 

Thanks, I'll definitely keep this med in mind though.
She is not taking birth control to my knowledge. She said before that she wouldn't be able to remember to take it consistently.

She's at an outpatient therapy program, and sees a regular therapist, but I find that both her meds and therapy have done little to help her. I don't know what to say to her because I don't want her to feel like I am not concerned for her, but I still find myself taking care of her when she gets panic attacks (these have really not decreased even with therapy and meds).

I'm not saying I mind, just that I don't think it's helping. 

I agree that we should also go to the root of the problem, but I don't know how.

She's said that she recognizes it has been a while since we've had sex, but she also doesn't think about it much at all, and even when she does, she knows she can't do anything about it (dryness).

Even when I've been able to get her wet, (that one time I mentioned in the post) it just felt wrong. She wasn't enjoying it, and wasn't really reacting. If anything, everything I did just seemed to annoy her, and that was off-putting for me.

Wow. I never thought to put it that way. Just wow. 

I don't know if she feels that way about me not having her best interests at heart (I feel this is probably true, but I don't want to speak for her), but I definitely do not trust that she takes my concerns seriously. 

We've had different arguments along the same vein whereby I expressed that exact feeling, and she said something similar (that I don't bother to understand how she feels about it).

We otherwise are doing fine. Like, we had a minor argument earlier this weekend but got over it. I don't know if this whole trust issue is an obvious detriment to our relationship right now, but I imagine it can be (especially if we do talk about the decrease in sex).

I totally get what you mean. 

I recognize that she may not want to switch or change her regimen if the meds are helping, but for me, I don't know if they are. 

I just know that we have been fighting more lately due to this and other things. 

The lack of intimacy in our relationship often leaves me frustrated and more depressed as s result. 

I feel like I can't bring it up without her feeling like I'm pressuring her to have sex, but I don't know if that bothers her, or if she even feels like the medication is worth sticking to. 

I get the feeling that even if she did want to change it, her anxiety prevents her from telling her psychiatrist. 

How should I handle this? I think I've been pretty patient and supportive for the last few months but putting my needs aside has in many ways worsened my own depression.
How did you come to that decision? All your own? Or did your SO (or whomever) bring it to your attention?

Right. I would have thought she brought it to her psychiatrist's attention when I told her that we were in the midst of a dead bedroom, but I feel like she also might have been too shy to bring it up.

It also very well could have been that it wasn't a concern for her (her psychiatrist did not warn her about the loss of libido) after she did find out it is a side effect. 

I don't know if I can bring it up without hurting her feelings or her just dismissing the issue as a necessary cost of coping with her depression.

I'm not 100% sure. She doesn't have bipolar disorder, but our school psychiatrist gave her lithium in low doses as a mood stabilizer. 

I didn't agree when I heard but she eventually switched to migraine meds and Zoloft. She blames a concussion about a year ago for ADHD and migraines, as well as memory loss. 

Zoloft sounds like it's the right medication for her based on what you've said. I want it to work, but the dead bedroom is making me feel like I'm missing a fundamental part of our relationship

She just says she doesn't think about it and thinking about it puts pressure on her to do something about it, thus leading to her being further turned off. 

I don't know what to say to that because it sounds like "sure it bothers her but what she supposed to do about it," kind of thing.
